A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Free PDF
signing FAQs.

The small print, without
the small print.

How can I add a signature to a PDF for free?+

Choose your PDF in the signing workspace, select Create signature, then draw or type your name. Place the signature on your chosen page and select Download PDF. There’s no account to create, payment to make, or watermark on your file. For a walkthrough, read how to sign a PDF for free.

Do I need to upload my PDF to a server?+

No. Your PDF stays in your browser. Inklet doesn’t send your document to a server. The page loads its code and fonts from web hosts, but your document isn’t sent to them. Download your signed copy before closing the page.

Can I sign a PDF with several pages?+

Yes. Use the page arrows to find the page you need and place your signature there. You can place one signature in the document at a time. Your downloaded PDF includes the other pages too.

Can I sign a PDF on my phone or tablet?+

Yes. Open Inklet in your browser, choose a PDF from your device, and draw with your finger or type your name. Drag your signature into place and download the signed file.

Can I draw or type my PDF signature?+

Both options are available. Draw a handwritten signature with your mouse, trackpad, or finger, or type your name and choose a signature style. You can use green, black, or blue ink. Read our guide to drawn and typed signatures to compare the options.

What PDF file sizes are supported?+

You can open PDF files up to 25 MB. If a file is larger, reduce its size before using Inklet. Password-protected or restricted PDFs may not open or save; ask the document owner for an editable copy.

Is this a certificate-based digital signature?+

No. Inklet adds an image of your handwritten or typed signature to your PDF. It doesn’t verify your identity, create a certificate-based digital signature, or provide an audit trail. Check what the recipient needs before signing.
